reviewContext.userProblem: riela events serve awaits every cron run inline, so a long run blocks all other sources in the process, and ticks missed during the run are silently coalesced into one later fire. No overlap policy exists anywhere in Sources at 3e6d4adf.
requiredOutcomes: Exactly four overlap policies: skip (default), cancelRunning, queue (bounded FIFO, default maxQueuedRuns 1, drop-newest overflow) and concurrent (optional maxConcurrentRuns, drop-newest overflow). Resolution is binding > workflow triggerDefaults > skip.
Cron runs execute as tracked tasks in CronOverlapDispatcher, keyed by bindingId. The serve loop never awaits cron runs except in --limit drain or shutdown.
Every outcome is recorded: one receipt per (tick, binding), overlap-* reasons, serve-record lastIgnoredReason and overlapPolicies, and riela events list reason=/binding= suffixes.

cancelRunning uses Task cancellation, waits up to a 30s settle bound, records the real runtime session ids and leaves no orphan process. The cancelled session ends as failed with failureKind cancelled.
--limit drains every accepted fire. Signal or error shutdown discards queued and pending fires (recorded as discarded) and cancels in-flight runs.

Routines: CLI and GraphQL can set the policy at create and through routine set-overlap-policy / setRoutineOverlapPolicy. Completion is counted once per successful run, and lastRunAt never moves backwards.
Validation diagnostics are verbatim per design §5.1 (INVALID_EVENT_OVERLAP_POLICY) and §5.2 (workflow.triggerDefaults). Configs without the fields keep validating and resolve to skip.
workflow inspect exposes triggerDefaults. The SDL is regenerated via scripts/surface-parity/generate-sdl.sh, and SurfaceParity is green.
nonGoals: No overlap policy for non-cron sources (webhooky, file-change, chat gateways stay inline).
No cross-process overlap control; workflow.loop.concurrency remains the cross-process guard.
No queue persistence; queued fires are in-memory and discarded on shutdown.
No edits to the riela-event-sources or riela-workflow skill docs, which live outside this repo (user-QA Q2, design §13).

Evidence records have integer exitStatus, testsRun and failureCount plus the full logPath.
Scratch and evidence files go under tmp/schedule-overlap-policy-20261021-session-471/<planId>/ only.
Same working directory, no worktrees, no git write operations by workers.

Tests use an injected manual clock and fake runners, not wall-clock sleeps. Session ids are runtime-store owned; the dispatcher only observes them.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Overlap scope key is bindingId: the policy is resolved per binding, a workflow-name key could mix bindings with different policies, and each routine owns exactly one binding (design §6.2).
Workflow-level default lives in a dedicated workflow.triggerDefaults object, not defaults, because it applies only to event-triggered dispatch; manual runs ignore it (design §4.2).
Policy values are decoded as raw strings so unknown values become validator diagnostics instead of decode failures, following the LoopConcurrencyDeclaration.onBusy precedent (design §4.1).
Resolution happens once at events serve startup; an unresolvable workflow falls back to skip with diagnostic overlap_policy_workflow_unresolved rather than failing serve (design §4.3).
dueTicks replaces dueTick: concurrent submits every due tick; the other policies submit the latest tick with explicit coalescedTickCount (design §6.3).

cancelRunning reuses Swift structured Task cancellation (the SIGINT/SIGTERM path) and LocalProcess process-group SIGKILL; a timed-out settle does not start the new run so runs never overlap (design §6.4, §8.1).
The session-start observer is placed outside the jsonlRecorder block in WorkflowRunCommand.runEventHandler because event-served runs use .json output (design §6.5, D13).
Read-only mode writes one read-only receipt per due tick and evaluates no overlap policy (design §7.1, D14).

Settle and shutdown waits are event-driven with generation-guarded timeout tasks and exactly-once stored continuations; racing with withTaskGroup is forbidden (plan 02, finding OVL-P02-SETTLE-RACE verified-fixed).
intentionalTradeoffs: Default skip changes prior implicit catch-up behavior (a one-slot queue via coalescing); operators wanting catch-up set overlapPolicy queue (design §4.4).
Cancelled runs are represented as status failed with failureKind cancelled instead of a new status case, pending user-QA Q1 confirmation (design §8.3).
Queue is in-memory only; pending entries are recorded as discarded on shutdown and not restored on restart (design §6.7).
cancelSettleTimeout is a fixed 30s constant, injectable only for tests (design §6.4).
Policy changes to routine bindings take effect at the next serve start, as with new routines today (design §9).
Inline non-cron runs can still delay cron tick evaluation; missed ticks are then handled by dueTicks coalescing rules (design §6.1).
supportedEdgeCases: skip with the running session id not yet known records overlap-skip:<bindingId>:pending.
concurrent cap overflow records overlap-concurrency-cap; queue overflow records overlap-queue-full (drop newest).
cancelRunning with an existing pending fire supersedes it (overlap-superseded); settle timeout records overlap-cancel-timeout and keeps the unsettled run tracked.
A run that completes before its cancellation takes effect is recorded completed and counted for its routine.
Routine gate is re-checked before deferred (queued or pending-after-cancel) starts; an inactive routine yields routine-<status>/routine-missing skip.
Out-of-order concurrent completions keep lastRunAt monotonic and runCount atomic.
Multiple bindings on one cron source get distinct per-(tick, binding) receipt ids.
--limit drain awaits in-flight, pending-after-cancel and queued fires; signal/error shutdown discards queued and pending fires and cancels in-flight runs.
workflow.loop.concurrency lease refusal of a second run surfaces as loop_concurrency_skipped recorded as failed.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Overlap between runs started by two separate events serve processes on the same event root.
Overlap between bindings that target the same workflow (handled only by workflow.loop.concurrency).
Overlap of webhooky, file-change or chat-gateway triggered runs.
Recovery of queued fires across a serve restart.
Runs still unsettled after the shutdown settle bound, which are left to the existing runtime finalizer and orphan handling.
